name.basis: the firm's own name on its site. Manager since 2014: Seedcamp Investment Management LLP (Companies House OC391626, incorporated 2014-03-04; FCA 628313; SEC exempt reporting adviser CRD 330799, SEC 802-130331; principal office 12 Little Portland Street, London W1W 8BJ). Earlier vehicles: Seedcamp Limited (06367351, 2007-09-11, dissolved 2020-11-24), Seedcamp Investments LLP (OC331184, Fund I) and Seedcamp Investments II LLP (OC355777, Fund II), both sold to Draper Esprit in October 2017 and dissolved 2025-06-17 (decisions.md D1).

investor_type.basis: a fund manager investing closed-end funds raised from institutions, founders and angels ('Seedcamp is a private investment fund', FAQs, read 2026-09-30); the same value every sibling profile carries.

website.basis: the firm's own site (WordPress; companies at /our-companies/, team at /our-team/, posts at /views/), read 2026-09-30.

icon_url.basis: NOT YET PUBLISHED: the value is the chosen source, replaced by the bucket URL when the icon is published at ingest (the Visionaries Club and HV Capital precedent), with `npx tsx scripts/fetch-investor-icon.ts seedcamp https://seedcamp.com/wp-content/themes/seedcamp/img/framework/safari-pinned-tab.svg --plate "#00FFAA"`. Chosen by measurement on 2026-09-30 (`--discover https://seedcamp.com`): the only square vector the site declares is the Safari mask icon (the firm's leaf mark, black on transparency, 500x500 intrinsic); the wide footer wordmark (1308x207) does not fit a round icon; android-chrome-192x192.png (the mark on a #00FFAA disc) refuses as a 1.34x enlargement (116px of artwork against the 155px the master needs); apple-touch-icon (180x180), favicon.ico (48x48) and the 32 and 16 px PNGs are too small; the manifest's 192 and 384 px icons 404. The plate #00FFAA is the site's own favicon disc colour (sampled from android-chrome-192x192.png: rgb(0,255,170), glyph rgb(30,53,45)). Dry run (`--dry-run`, nothing uploaded): svg 500x500 (vector, rendered at 2x), 154px in the 256px master (1.00x); safe area already within the keyline (box 60%, radius 70%); master 256x256 opaque-plate rgb(4,252,172) opaque=100% box=60% radius=70% contrast=14.4:1 ramp=0.76px. With the default plate the same source gives a white plate at 18.4:1; the brand plate matches the site's favicon.

founding_year.basis: the firm's own boilerplate (post of 2016-06-09): 'Seedcamp was founded in 2007 by Reshma Sohoni with Saul Klein and a number of European investors'; the first applications opened in July 2007 and the first six companies were announced on 2007-09-07 (Views posts); Seedcamp Limited was incorporated 2007-09-11 and Seedcamp Investments LLP (Fund I) 2007-09-07 (Companies House; decisions.md D1).

history.value: Seedcamp was founded in London in 2007 by Saul Klein and Reshma Sohoni, with a €2.5 million fund that backed teams chosen at its Seedcamp events. It was among the first investors in Wise, Revolut, UiPath and Synthesia. In 2026 it raised $320 million for its seventh flagship fund and its Select fund for later rounds, and it now manages about $1 billion.
history.basis: founders and year: the firm's post of 2016-06-09 ('founded in 2007 by Reshma Sohoni with Saul Klein') and a press clipping of 2008-07-28 (Tim Bradshaw) quoted in the firm's post of 2008-08-04 ('Founded by Saul Klein of Index Ventures and run by Reshma Sohoni'); the first fund: 'a tiny micro-fund ... with 2.5MEuros in cash' ('Introducing Seedcamp V', 2020-11-11); the programme origin: Seedcamp Week in London and the Mini Seedcamps, EUR 50K per chosen team (decisions.md D2, D3); the four bets: 'Seedcamp was the first believer in Revolut, Wise, UiPath, Synthesia and Fluidstack' (Fund VII post, 2026-06-19), each a company in the portfolio (Wise entered 2011 from Fund II, Revolut and UiPath 2015, Synthesia 2019); today: '$320 million in new funds ... $220 million for Fund VII, our flagship first-check fund and $100 million for our Select fund' (2026-06-19) and '$1 billion in assets under management' (TechCrunch, 2026-06-22). Moved here from the page: the fund ladder (EUR 2.5M, EUR 5M, EUR 20M, GBP 60M, GBP 78M, $180M, $220M); the sale of Funds I and II to Draper Esprit in October 2017 at a 4x return (post of 2017-10-25); the co-founder Saul Klein was a partner at Index Ventures from 2009 and later co-founded LocalGlobe (decisions.md D8), and Carlos Eduardo Espinal (at the firm from 2010) runs it with Sohoni as Managing Partner; the firm takes board observer roles, not board seats (FAQs).

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own words, verbatim from the homepage headline (the page's only h1), read 2026-09-30; the same line is the page's meta description and og:description. The site sets it as 'By Your Side from Day One': sentence case, curly quotes and a closing period are the only edits. Competing lines on the same site, not used: the FAQs' 'We are your first backer.' and 'We remain Europe's original first check investor', and the footer strapline 'Unrivalled network • Unfiltered advice • Unwavering support'. Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: the firm's own words: first cheques at pre-seed and seed ('We are your first backer. The companies we partner with range from pre-product and pre-revenue to post-launch ... If you have already raised more than a couple of million dollars, we're probably not the right fit', FAQs, read 2026-09-30; Fund VI: 'first cheques of up to $1M in Angel to Seed rounds', post of 2023-05-16); follow-ons from the flagship funds' reserves 'in rounds up to Series B' (Fund IV post, 2017-11-22) -> Series A; the Select fund 'to back our portfolio winners as they scale through Series B and beyond' (FAQs; $3M to $5M per check in Series B rounds and later, TechCrunch 2026-06-22) -> Growth. Series A and Growth are follow-on stages only; the firm does not enter there. Landed entry stages on the grind (classification.json, 567 members, 2026-09-30): Pre-Seed 296, Seed 73, Growth 1 (Function Health, a Select entry, decisions.md D5), undetermined 197. Encoded as the siblings with an opportunity or follow-on vehicle (Cherry, Point Nine, Creandum).

investment_geo.basis: the firm's own words: 'we tend to focus on investing in companies based in Europe and Israel, or companies with a distinctively European angle' (FAQs, read 2026-09-30), with a US team and a New York office to help European founders who move west (FAQs; Fund VII post, 2026-06-19). The landed portfolio's hq_country (classification.json, 567 members): 510 in Europe (GB 295, FR 53, DE 38, ES 15, PT 10, DK 10 and 25 more countries), US 37, IL 11, other 9 -> core Europe; other US (by the portfolio, mostly European founders who moved) and Israel (by the firm's own words). Core respects the two-label cap.

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 439 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 20 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: lower: the firm's own first cheque, 'Our first cheque is usually between $350K-$1.25M' (FAQs, read 2026-09-30; the same answer read '$350K-$1M' from 2020-12-01, decisions.md D3) = $350,000. median: press-based, the median of 63 entry rounds the firm announced in its own posts with a stated size, each post the row's entry citation on the grind (2016 to 2026; non-USD sizes converted at the ECB rate of the post date with scripts/fx-convert.py) = $2,713,500, published $2.7M; quartiles $1.6M / $3.5M; by stage Pre-Seed $2.6M over 34, Seed $3.0M over 29. It is a round size, not the firm's cheque, and fair only because the firm leads or co-leads many of these rounds. Posts left out because they announce a later round than the entry, or cover several rounds: yonder (post announces the £20M round after the £850K pre-seed the firm led (Feb 2021)); vyne (post announces the $15.5M round after the pre-seed the firm led (Nov 2019)); riskbook (post announces the £2M round after the pre-seed the firm led); sylvera (post announces the $7.8M seed after the firm's pre-seed); fullview (post announces the seed six months after the firm's pre-seed); light (post announces a follow-on in the $13M round); embedd (post (2026) announces a round after the 2023 entry); murphy (post covers $15M across pre-seed and seed with existing investors, the entry share unstated); primer (post announces the £3.8M round after the pre-seed the firm led; the pre-seed size is not stated); argil (post (2024-11) is a year after the 2023 entry); emma (post (2025-12) is two years after the 2023 entry); uncovr (post (2026-06) is a year after the 2025 entry); botika (post (2025-01) announces the $8M seed two years after the 2023 entry). The pre-2016 programme entries carry the standard cheque of their era (EUR 50K for 8-10%, then EUR 75K for 7%, GBP 100K for 7.5%) and no round size, so they are not in the median. No Form D distribution: the companies are European and file none (decisions.md D8). upper: the Select fund's cheque, 'about $3 million to $5 million per check, following on in Series B rounds and later' (TechCrunch, 2026-06-22) = $5,000,000. Cross-checks: Fund VII's first cheque is 'roughly $1 million' (TechCrunch, same article); the largest entry rounds the firm led or co-led in its own posts are Prelude's $8M seed (co-led with Singular, 2024-11-14) and Lupin & Holmes' $5.9M pre-seed (co-led with 20VC, 2026-03-17), round sizes rather than cheques; a 10-15% single-position cap on Fund VII ($220M) is $22M to $33M for a whole position and does not bind. Rejected as range ends: BioOrbit's $13.2M seed (2026-04-30, the firm a participant, no lead stated) and Function Health's $298M Series B (Select joined; Redpoint led).

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24); each is a member row in the ledger (verdict member, 2026-09-30) and appears on the firm's homepage or in its own 'first believer' list (Fund VII post, 2026-06-19). Considered next: Sorare, Pleo, Fluidstack, 9fin, Function Health.

aum.basis: bottom: the sworn Form ADV Section 7.B(1) gross asset values of the firm's only adviser, Seedcamp Investment Management LLP, exempt reporting adviser, CRD 330799 (annual amendment signed 2026-06-25, fiscal year ending March; IAPD PDF sources/registers/adv-330799.pdf parsed page by page with pypdf, 'Total Funds: 8', deduped by private fund ID): Seedcamp III L.P. $316,059,102; Seedcamp IV L.P. $333,937,334; Seedcamp V L.P. $125,948,848; Seedcamp VI L.P. $114,936,381; the four opportunity vehicles SC_3_OF1 LP $11,982,196, SC_3_OF4 LP $17,785,662, SC_4_OF1 LP $11,505,319, SC_4_OF2 LP $2,672,354; total $934,827,196. An exempt reporting adviser files no Item 5.F, so the 7.B composite is the sworn figure (Creandum, Balderton precedent). It is a floor: Fund VII ($220M) and the $100M Select fund, announced 2026-06-19, are not among its eight funds, and Funds I and II (sold to Draper Esprit in 2017) never reported to the SEC. top: press, 'It has 12 unicorns in its portfolio of more than 550 companies and $1 billion in assets under management' (TechCrunch, 2026-06-22, https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/22/seedcamp-raises-320m-for-its-new-fund-to-expand-its-us-footprint/); Vestbee (2026-06-22) says 'more than $1 billion'; the only credible press figure (Cherry precedent: an ERA whose ADV lags the fund ladder anchors only the bottom). Adding the $320M of new commitments to the gross asset values would give $1.25B, but that mixes marked value with committed capital, so it is not published.

funds.basis: sizes from the firm's own posts, non-USD figures converted at the ECB rate of the announcement date (scripts/fx-convert.py): Seedcamp VII $220M and Seedcamp Select $100M ('Fund VII is now live', 2026-06-19; TechCrunch 2026-06-22; the Select strategy was already investing by 2025-11-20, Function Health's Series B 'via our Select fund', and the $100M fund is not on the June 2026 ADV, so its vintage is the 2026 announcement); Seedcamp VI $180M ('Welcome to Seedcamp VI', 2023-05-16; Seedcamp VI L.P., LP022863); Seedcamp V GBP 78M @ ECB 2020-11-11 (GBP/EUR 0.88935, EUR/USD 1.1766) = $103,193,119 ('Introducing Seedcamp V', 2020-11-11); Seedcamp IV GBP 60M final close @ ECB 2018-05-23 (GBP/EUR 0.87953, EUR/USD 1.1708) = $79,869,931 (post of 2018-05-23; first close GBP 41M on 2017-11-22, first investment Pace 2017-12-14, so vintage 2017); Seedcamp III EUR 20M @ ECB 2014-07-15 (EUR/USD 1.3613) = $27,226,000 (the firm's own figure, 'our last (EUR 20M raised in 2014)', post of 2017-11-22; the launch post of 2014-07-15 said 'a new fund, worth more than $30m' and TechCrunch the same day reported a $28M first close of a $30M target, 49.9% from the EIF); Seedcamp II (Seedcamp Investments II LLP) EUR 5M @ ECB 2011-09-08 (1.4044) = $7,022,000 ('Seedcamp's fund is now at EUR 5M', post of 2011-09-08; first close EUR 3M announced 2010-11-16); Seedcamp I (Seedcamp Investments LLP) EUR 2.5M @ ECB 2007-09-07 (1.3696) = $3,424,000 ('2.5MEuros in cash', post of 2020-11-11; no dated announcement exists, so the rate is that of the vehicle's formation and the first six investments, 2007-09-07; the 2018 post's '$2.5M' is a slip for EUR). No entry carries an accession: the only own Form D is Seedcamp V L.P. (CIK 1830158, 2020q4), an 'Indefinite' offering with $9,200,080 sold, the US investors' part only. Not listed, counted here: the four opportunity vehicles on the ADV (SC_3_OF1, SC_3_OF4, SC_4_OF1, SC_4_OF2 LP, $43.9M of gross assets), the GP LLPs and founder partnerships, Seedcamp VI Investments Ltd (2025) and Seedcamp VII Investments Ltd (2026), and the AngelList syndicate series 'AL-Seedcamp-Funds' (not the firm's funds, decisions.md D6). Funds I and II were sold to Draper Esprit in October 2017 (post of 2017-10-25).

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 12 Little Portland Street, London, United Kingdom (SEEDCAMP INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT LLP, CRD 330799, Annual Amendment filed 2026-06-25). The firm's site lists London, United Kingdom; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
